name: Idaho
overview: Idaho does not sell tax liens. If delinquent property taxes aren't paid within three years, the county tax collector issues a tax deed to the county. The county commissioners then auction the property, within 14 months of the tax deed, to the highest bidder, with a minimum bid that covers the taxes, interest and costs owed. Money left over after the county is paid goes to parties in interest and then to the former owner. Property the county can't sell at auction may later be sold without further notice. In Canyon County the former owner can redeem right up until the parcel is offered, so parcels often drop off the list.

overview_sources.quote: If real property on which there is a delinquency is not redeemed within three (3) years from the date of delinquency, the county tax collector of the county wherein such property is situated must make, in favor of said county, a tax deed for such property.
For tax deeded property, the board of county commissioners shall conduct an auction no later than fourteen (14) months from the issuance of the tax deed.
The property shall be sold to the highest bidder.
the board of county commissioners shall set the minimum bid for the tax deeded property to include all property taxes owing, interest and costs
** PREVIOUS OWNERS CAN REDEEM PROPERTY UP TO THE TIME THEIR PROPERTY IS OFFERED FOR SALE AT PUBLIC AUCTION.
